Token release policy

Vesting that users can understand before they buy.

PHN uses fixed supply, separated operating buckets, visible contract addresses and staged release logic. This page explains what is live, what is funded, and what needs governance or admin action.

Allocation clarity

Launch allocation view

BucketAmountRelease modelUser meaning
Founder vesting40M PHN target after staking redirectionLinear vesting policy, no sudden public-market release.Team incentives stay long term.
Staking rewards10M PHN fundedDistributed through PHNStaking per tier and elapsed time.Rewards come from a known pool, not hidden minting.
Node rewards20M PHNReserved for verified node operators and heartbeat-based rewards.Node earning requires identity and activity checks.
Ecosystem and growth20M PHN base bucketListings, grants, partnerships, support and operations.Used to grow peaq-first adoption.
Liquidity10M PHN base bucketLiquidity provisioning and market route support.Pairs must be created and locked transparently.

Note: the deployed token originally minted fixed buckets on-chain. The operating plan now redirects 10M PHN into the staking reward pool, which is why the public tokenomics page separates staking from the original founder bucket.

Presale

Buyer delivery

Presale buyers receive PHN through the presale contract. Epoch pricing starts at $0.02, then advances by cap. Purchase fee is 2% total: 0.25% burn and 1.75% treasury.

Open presale
Staking

Reward unlocks

Flex rewards can be claimed without a lock. Locked and Vault tiers pay higher APY for time commitment and use penalty rules for early exit.

Team release

Founder release is tracked separately and should remain visible through explorer links and future governance reports.

Recommended governance controls

What should happen before scale

Publish monthly treasury report

Report balances for presale, staking, liquidity and ecosystem wallets.

Lock liquidity after pair creation

LP tokens should be locked for a clear period and linked from the verify page.

Use timelock for privileged actions

Critical admin actions should be delayed and publicly visible before execution.
